description: ¡Hola! Soy estudiante,busco formar un equipo para el desafío de monitoreo de la salud de astronautas. La idea es desarrollar un software que integre datos de sensores y dispositivos para visualizar el estado de salud y detectar cambios relevantes durante una misión. Busco personas interesadas en programación, hardware, IA, análisis de datos y áreas de salud. Quiero formar un equipo multidisciplinario y de manera virtual.
summary:
SIMISA is a digital platform designed for the comprehensive monitoring of astronauts’ health during long-duration space missions.

The project aims to centralize indicators from different systems of the human body through an interactive interface that allows users to monitor cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic, and skeletal health, as well as sleep, rest, and psychological well-being.

The platform integrates data collection, organization, and validation; the display of graphs and historical data; the identification of relevant changes; and an intelligent assistant that provides informational support. It also includes distinct profiles for astronauts, medical personnel, and researchers, as well as local data storage and synchronization with Earth when communication is available.

The prototype aims to help astronauts understand their health status, review their vital signs, and access support information during missions where assistance from Earth may be limited by distance and communication delays.
details:
What does SIMISA do?

SIMISA integrates various functions for monitoring and tracking astronauts’ health into a single platform.

It allows users to view physiological indicators, review information by body system, record measurements, visualize trends, check alerts, and access support information through a supervised intelligent assistant.

Its interface features an interactive human figure that makes it easy to explore different body regions and their related indicators.

How does it work?

The system consists of four main processes:

  1. Data collection and reception. It collects information through manual entries and simulated data in the prototype, with an architecture designed for future integration with sensors and devices.
  2. Organization and validation. Each measurement is organized by its indicator, value, unit, date, time, source, and quality status. This allows for the identification of incomplete, invalid, or outdated information.
  3. Monitoring and analysis. It displays indicators, trend graphs, history, and alerts for significant changes, taking into account personal reference values and data availability.
  4. Assistance and Communication. The smart assistant makes it easier to understand indicators and access approved information and procedures. The platform includes local storage and the ability to prepare records for synchronization with the medical team on Earth.

What benefits does it offer?

  • It centralizes information from different body systems.
  • It facilitates individual monitoring of indicators.
  • It allows users to review trends and relevant changes.
  • It organizes the history of measurements.
  • It distinguishes between sensor issues and health-related alerts.
  • It facilitates access to support information.
  • It is designed to operate without a continuous connection to Earth.
  • It offers different views depending on the user type.

What does it hope to achieve?

SIMISA aims to contribute to greater autonomy in monitoring astronauts’ health during long-duration space missions.

The platform is expected to facilitate the identification of changes, the retrieval of relevant information, and the organization of data to support the astronaut and the medical team.

The project will be able to evolve through the integration of real sensors, more advanced analysis methods, a 3D anatomical model, and a supervised medical knowledge base.

Tools and Technologies Used

To develop SIMISA, we used the following tools and technologies:

  • Interface design and prototyping: artificial intelligence tools such as Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, and other visual support tools to explore, organize, and improve design proposals.
  • Interface development: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
  • Server development: Node.js.
  • Data management: local files managed via Node.js.
  • Version control and collaboration: GitHub and Discord.

We did not use any medical hardware or physical sensors at this stage; the project was developed as a software prototype.

Creativity and Innovation in the Project

SIMISA’s creativity lies in integrating into a single platform various elements that are normally separate: health indicator tracking, visualization of the human body, measurement history, alerts, sleep and well-being tracking, and an intelligent support assistant.

In addition, SIMISA takes into account the specific conditions of long-duration space missions, such as distance from Earth, communication challenges, and the need for health information during periods without connectivity.
